dimensions.name: Contract extraction & environment probing

evidence.note: Environment probing before building: checks python3 version, pip, whether uvicorn/gunicorn are installed, then installs the needed dependency set (fastapi, uvicorn, aiosqlite, websockets, jinja2). Confirms runtime/language/framework and ports plan early.

Extracts and verifies explicit contract details: token length >=16, status codes 409 (duplicate), 400 (invalid username/short password), 401 (wrong password). Confirms envelope shapes {user, token}, {workspace, general_channel} match spec.
Catches specific contract shapes — reactions as [{emoji,count,user_ids}], node_id 0/1/2 indexing per port — showing targeted reading of the spec's exact shapes rather than a vague Slack model.

Repeated systematic data-testid audits against the pinned selector list (counting present vs missing: channel-entry, new-channel-btn, channel-member-row, etc.), plus catching subtle traps: mention exclusion by workspace membership, prompt()/confirm() ban for browser grading, read-state membership checks. This is genuine targeted contract mining beyond obvious CRUD.

Extracts invariant-level requirements: dense per-channel seq across mixed writers, the 5-second resilience window on broadcast-kill (drives adding a DB event_queue polling fallback). Research steers implementation order here.

No distilled, written contract inventory is maintained; research lives in per-step analysis prose. Several subtle traps never surface: guest/member/admin channel-creation gates, transfer_ownership vs PATCH-to-owner rejection, /me & /shrug literal body semantics, topic not auto-populated, resume.gap frame — so coverage of sharp edges is partial.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly probes the runtime (python/pip/deps/ports, later discovering nc unavailable) and extracts the main contracts per subsystem with explicit status codes and envelope keys — squarely meeting the level-5 anchor. It goes beyond that by repeatedly auditing the pinned testid list and catching several subtle invariants (non-member mention exclusion, dense-seq-across-writers, the 5s broadcast-kill window, node_id indexing, no prompt/confirm), pushing toward level 8. But it never distills a referenced/living contract inventory and misses a cluster of the spec's sharp edges (role gating, transfer-ownership-vs-PATCH, slash-command literal semantics, topic default, resume.gap), so it falls short of the systematic level-8 description. This lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestone structure

evidence.note: Early architecture decision names the shared substrate as central: 3 HTTP processes + IRC + cross-node broadcast hub 'coordinated via shared database and direct inter-node communication', and start.sh/supervisor designed as a first-class piece early rather than bolted on — recognizing seq store and fan-out transport as prerequisites.

Dependency-correct ordering in practice: DB → server API → auth tested → workspaces/channels → messages/reactions/threads → each subsystem gets an implicit 'it works' curl check before moving on; API validated before the SPA is rewritten.
SPA rewrite and cluster launch sequenced after the API core is verified working, showing foundations-before-dependents ordering (API before UI).

Resilience fan-out (DB event_queue polling as fallback for peer WebSocket) was added reactively late in the build when the agent realized the broadcast-kill requirement, rather than isolated as its own early milestone with exit criteria — this is what keeps it below the 8/10 anchor.

Resilience/node-kill treated as a near-final verification milestone rather than an early load-bearing milestone; the per-step 'Plan:' notes are next-action notes, not an explicit milestone hierarchy with written per-milestone acceptance checks.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent followed a sensible, dependency-aware order (env probe → DB → API → per-feature checks → SPA → clustering/resilience) and recognized the critical shared substrate (dense per-channel seq, cross-node transport) and start.sh supervision early, matching the level-5 anchor's 'ordered breakdown into major subsystems with implicit it-works checks' and early substrate recognition. It falls short of level 8 because there is no explicit milestone hierarchy with written per-milestone acceptance criteria, and the highest-risk cross-cutting invariant (broadcast-kill fan-out survival) was handled reactively/bolted-on late rather than isolated as an early milestone with concrete exit criteria.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification across protocols

evidence.note: Systematic curl/HTTP tests asserting exact status codes (201/409/400/401), envelope shapes for auth, channels, messages, reactions, threads — genuine self-built checks reproducing grader probes.
Python socket tests for IRC (PASS/NICK/USER→welcome, JOIN/TOPIC/NAMES) and cross-node WebSocket event propagation with seq-consistency check — spanning IRC and WS transports.
Comprehensive Python integration script covering files (413/download), archive (423), groups, invitations, DMs; confirmed dense seq. Broad main-path coverage across subsystems.
Actively SIGKILLed HTTP node 8000 and verified reads/writes continued on 8001/8002 plus supervisor auto-restart — a real adversarial resilience probe (part of the level-8 behavior).

SPA verification was only static grep/count of data-testid strings in served HTML, never a real browser pass; and the broadcast-kill fallback (steps 65-67) was built but never killed-and-re-verified for 5s seq density.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built reusable curl/Python checks across HTTP, WebSocket, and IRC, confirmed many exact status codes and envelope shapes, verified cross-node seq consistency, and — beyond the level-5 anchor — actually SIGKILLed an HTTP node and confirmed continued service plus restart. However it never drove a real browser (SPA was only grepped for testids), never tested the broadcast-component kill it had engineered, and never checked resume.gap or mixed HTTP+IRC dense-seq. That places it clearly above 5 but well below the full four-transport-plus-both-failure-injections bar of 8, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface

evidence.note: Maintains explicit enumerated 'remaining issues' lists (missing testids, prompt/confirm usage, cross-node fan-out unverified, mentions filtering, group mention resolution, read-state) — subsystem-granular done-vs-remaining tracking early in the build.

Repeatedly cross-checks the served SPA against the spec's ~80 testid list by counting them ('63 unique data-testid attributes'), names specific missing ones (channel-entry, new-channel-btn, channel-settings-title, channel-member-row/add-member) and drives them to closure — direct contract-list cross-check so features aren't silently dropped.
Detects a whole missing capability (DB-polling fallback for the broadcast-kill 5s window) that wasn't yet built, and adds it — catching an omission before finishing rather than after.

Revisits the mention regex thinking it's broken, then correctly recognizes it was only the file-read representation and the code was fine — avoids a wasted 'fix' loop; a mild self-correction rather than an explicit named stuck-state.

Runs a comprehensive end-to-end test sweep across auth, workspaces, channels, messages/threads/reactions, DMs, files, groups, invitations, IRC, cross-node seq, and resilience (node kill) — uses results to update the ledger (e.g. reasons through the search '0 results' and DELETE-204 test artifacts rather than blindly re-debugging).
Final status summary itemizes each subsystem and its verification state, showing a sustained (if prose-based, not tool-tracked) done-vs-remaining picture at the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains a subsystem-granular, continuously-restated ledger of done/partial/remaining work in its Analysis/Plan prose, and crucially cross-checks it against concrete spec contract lists (the testid catalogue, status codes, resilience window), catching omissions like the DB-polling fallback and missing testids before finishing — clearly above the level-5 anchor. It falls short of 8-10 because the tracking is informal prose rather than an explicit maintained status artifact, and it only weakly detects/naming of stuck or circular states (it did avoid one wasted regex fix, but revisited seq atomicity and testids repeatedly without ever explicitly flagging thrashing). That places it at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified design assumptions

evidence.note: DM workspace_id FK crash diagnosed (sentinel 'system' user missing) and fixed at root cause rather than papered over — a targeted correction driven by reading the crash log.

Re-reading the broadcast-kill resilience requirement, the agent adds a DB event_queue polling path as a fan-out fallback — a genuine design-level addition, but bolted on proactively rather than triggered by an observed test failure.
Recognizes get_next_seq's UPDATE-then-SELECT is not truly atomic and simplifies it; investigates mention regex escaping — design-aware reconsideration of correctness-critical components.

Runs the SIGKILL-a-node resilience test and confirms the other nodes keep serving; but the broadcast-component-kill invariant (dense seq within 5s of broadcaster loss) is never actually injected/verified — the added fallback is asserted, not stress-tested.

Sequence of targeted bug fixes (IRC import, SPA path resolution) each diagnosed from logs/curl output rather than retried blindly, but all symptom-local fixes without questioning the underlying architecture.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnoses failures and makes targeted, root-cause corrections rather than blind retries or sleeps (steps 28-30, 42-52), and occasionally reconsiders component-level design (adding a DB event-queue fan-out fallback at 64-66, fixing non-atomic seq at 67-69) — matching anchor 5. It falls short of anchor 8 because the highest-risk invariant (dense seq / fan-out survival under broadcast-component kill) was anticipated and patched but never actually falsification-tested; the resilient seq authority (shared DB) was an upfront choice rather than a re-architecture prompted by a divergent test result.

dimensions.name: Grader-value scope triage under budget

evidence.note: Chose shared SQLite (WAL) across all 3 nodes — a deliberate architectural call that cheaply satisfies cross-node consistency and dense seq, de-risking two high-coverage invariants early.
Recognized that prompt()/confirm() would fail the automated browser grader and prioritized a full SPA rewrite with forms/modals — targeting a heavily-graded flow over polish.
Repeated audits of the grader-pinned data-testid set and token hydration, front-loading UI invariants that gate many browser checks.
Added DB event-queue polling specifically to meet the 5-second cross-node fan-out resilience window — consciously addressing a graded resilience invariant.
Simulated the SIGKILL resilience scenario and verified other nodes kept serving, reflecting awareness of which subsystems the grader stresses.
Final summary enumerates the load-bearing graded systems (nodes, IRC numerics, testids, seq, resilience) but shows no explicit deferral/minimal-viable calls on lower-value features.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly did more than implicit ordering (above 3) and roughly targeted the big-ticket graded areas first (5): auth/API, then SPA, then IRC/cluster, then resilience. Beyond that, it repeatedly reasoned about likely grader coverage — the browser grader's dislike of prompts, the pinned data-testids, the 5s broadcast-kill window, and dense seq — and front-loaded those invariants (pushing toward 8). But the work is largely reactive bug-fixing rather than a revisited value/risk allocation, and it makes no explicit 'minimal viable' or deferral decisions on lower-yield features, so it falls short of the 8/10 anchors. Level 6 fits.

rubric.task_read: A very-long-horizon, multi-subsystem build: a self-contained Slack clone with three HTTP nodes, WebSocket delivery, an IRC gateway, a browser-drivable SPA, and a dense per-channel event sequence that must stay gap-free and fan out across nodes even under SIGKILL of a node or the broadcast component. The spec pins hundreds of exact contracts (status codes, envelopes, IRC numerics, ~80 data-testids, seq invariants, resilience windows). Difficulty comes from enormous breadth, many hard-to-fake distributed-systems invariants, and an opaque grader — so heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work (contract extraction, milestone structure, self-built verification, failure-mode testing) is decisive rather than optional.

dimensions.name: Contract extraction & environment probing
dimensions.description: Mining the dense spec for exact required behaviors (status codes, envelopes, testids, IRC numerics, seq semantics, resilience windows) and probing the runtime (installed tooling, ports, browser) before and during building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader asserts precise shapes across HTTP/WS/IRC/UI; a single mis-read contract (e.g. `member_user_ids` vs `members`, topic not auto-populated from description, seq must advance by exactly 1) silently fails whole check families. Blind coding here guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts coding from a vague 'Slack clone' mental model; never returns to the spec for exact shapes; ignores the testid/numeric/seq lists.
anchors.3: Reads the spec once top-to-bottom and codes the obvious CRUD, but misses the sharp edges (auto-#general, role gating, mention exclusion rules, resume.gap, node_id indexing) and never checks what's installed.
anchors.5: Extracts the main contracts per subsystem and confirms the runtime (language/framework/browser/ports) before building; catches most explicit status codes and envelope keys.
anchors.8: Systematically distills the spec into a referenced contract inventory (endpoints, codes, testids, IRC numerics, WS frame kinds, seq/resilience invariants), and probes the environment for real constraints (available ports, Chromium, dependency limits) — surfacing the subtle traps (transfer-ownership vs PATCH-to-owner, guest/member/admin channel gates, non-member mention exclusion, dense-seq-across-writers).
anchors.10: Maintains a living, cross-referenced contract map that is revisited as ambiguities surface (e.g. how DM idempotency, tombstoned-reaction counting, or resume.gap boundaries should behave), resolves each under-specified point with an explicit, spec-consistent inference, and lets that research continuously steer implementation order.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the system into ordered, independently-verifiable subsystems (auth → workspaces/channels → messages/threads/reactions → WS → IRC → SPA → clustering/resilience) each with an explicit done-check, and sequencing them so foundations exist before dependents.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is far too large for one undifferentiated push; without a dependency-aware milestone plan the agent risks building the SPA before the API works or resilience before the seq layer exists, and cannot tell what fraction is truly complete.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features reactively; foreground start.sh and clustering treated as afterthoughts.
anchors.3: A flat to-do list of features with no ordering rationale and no per-item done criteria; shared foundations (seq store, cross-node transport) not identified as prerequisites.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered breakdown into major subsystems with rough milestones, each with an implicit 'it works' check; the critical shared substrate (durable per-channel seq, fan-out transport) is recognized early.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone hierarchy with per-milestone acceptance checks, dependencies made visible (auth/token before everything; seq+persistence before WS/IRC/resilience; API before SPA), and start.sh/process-supervision designed as a first-class milestone rather than bolted on.
anchors.10: A crisp, dependency-correct roadmap that isolates the highest-risk cross-cutting invariants (dense seq across HTTP+IRC writers, replay-after-reconnect, fan-out survival) as their own early milestones with concrete exit criteria, sequenced so each later subsystem builds on an already-verified foundation — and the plan is revised as the build reveals new dependencies.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification across protocols
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks the grader won't hand you: curl/HTTP assertions on codes and envelopes, WebSocket subscribe/resume/seq tests, IRC socket sessions, SPA driving, and — critically — actively simulating the SIGKILL and broadcast-kill resilience scenarios.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is opaque and covers HTTP+WS+IRC+browser+failure injection. Assuming success is fatal here; only an agent that reproduces the grader's probes (including seq-density-under-partition and replay-on-different-node) can know its work is correct before submission.

anchors.0: No verification beyond 'the server starts'; never exercises endpoints, WS frames, IRC, the UI, or any failure scenario.
anchors.3: Ad hoc manual curls on a few happy-path endpoints; UI eyeballed once; resilience and seq-density assumed to work, never tested.
anchors.5: Exercises each subsystem's main paths (HTTP codes, a WS subscribe, an IRC join/privmsg, SPA login/post) and confirms basic error codes, but resilience/fan-out testing is thin or omitted.
anchors.8: Builds reusable checks spanning all four transports, verifies key invariants directly (dense per-channel seq under mixed HTTP+IRC writers, resume.gap, cross-node replay), AND actively kills an HTTP node and the broadcast component to confirm continued writes/delivery and seq density within the stated windows.
anchors.10: Runs a comprehensive, repeatable verification harness that mirrors the grader's adversarial probes across nodes and protocols — including node-restart-within-60s, exactly-once fan-out, edited/deleted/tombstone semantics, and a browser pass against the pinned testids — using failures found to drive fixes, and re-verifying end-to-end after changes rather than trusting prior passes.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface
dimensions.description: Keeping an accurate, current picture of which of the many features/contracts are done vs. remaining vs. broken across a long build, and detecting stuck or circular states (e.g. re-debugging seq gaps repeatedly).
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of endpoints, ~80 testids, and several invariants, it is easy to lose the plot, silently drop whole feature families, or thrash on one hard bug while the rest rots. Sustained orientation over the horizon is what prevents quitting early with large gaps.

anchors.0: No sense of overall completion; forgets whole subsystems (IRC, search, groups, read-state) or repeats the same failed fix without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers late that major areas were never built; no signal for being stuck.
anchors.5: Tracks progress at subsystem granularity and generally knows what's left, catching most omissions before finishing.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, continuously-updated status of features/contracts (done / partial / failing), notices when a fix isn't converging and names the stuck state, and uses that ledger to decide what to touch next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise done-vs-remaining map across the entire surface for the whole horizon, cross-checks it against the spec's contract list so nothing is silently dropped, and reliably detects thrashing/circular debugging early enough to switch tactics rather than burn the budget.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified design assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the architecture or approach when reality diverges — e.g. the chosen cross-node transport can't preserve dense seq under the broadcast-kill, or replay-on-different-node exposes a persistence/ordering flaw — instead of pushing ahead on a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Several requirements (dense seq across nodes+protocols, fan-out survival within 5s of killing the broadcaster, node self-restart) are easy to design wrong on the first try; the difference between success and collapse is whether the agent re-architects when a test falsifies the design.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps a design that demonstrably violates seq density or resilience and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally (retries, sleeps) without questioning a flawed transport/persistence design; recurring failures persist.
anchors.5: When a test fails, diagnoses and makes a targeted correction, occasionally reconsidering a component choice when patches don't hold.
anchors.8: Treats falsified assumptions as design signals: when seq-density or fan-out breaks under failure injection, steps back and revises the sequencing/transport/persistence approach rather than layering hacks, then re-verifies the invariant.
anchors.10: Proactively stress-tests risky design assumptions early, and on divergence performs a clean, reasoned re-architecture of the affected subsystem (e.g. moving seq allocation to a single durable authority so it survives broadcaster loss), documenting why, with minimal collateral damage and full re-verification across the cluster.

dimensions.name: Grader-value scope triage under budget
dimensions.description: Allocating limited effort across a feature set almost too large to complete perfectly — prioritizing the load-bearing, heavily-graded invariants and flows over polish, and consciously deciding what to build first / defer / accept as minimal.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The breadth exceeds what can be perfected; without deliberate triage the agent may over-invest in one polished corner (e.g. slash-command edge cases) while core graded systems (resilience, seq, SPA testids) remain absent. Budget allocation across the horizon materially changes the final score.

anchors.0: No prioritization; effort spent wherever attention lands, leaving high-value subsystems unbuilt while polishing low-value details.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; over- or under-invests in areas without weighing grader coverage.
anchors.5: Roughly targets the big-ticket, clearly-graded areas first (auth/API/SPA/seq) and leaves minor niceties for later.
anchors.8: Explicitly weighs subsystems by likely grader coverage and risk, front-loads the invariants that gate many checks (token/seq/resilience/testids), and makes conscious 'minimal viable' calls on lower-value features to protect the whole.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited value/risk allocation across the full horizon — sequencing so the highest-coverage, highest-risk systems are solid early, deferring or stubbing low-yield features intentionally, and reallocating budget as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most score.
